about.title: About JalTaap
about.lead: JalTaap is a WhatsApp-first safety copilot for Delhi's outdoor workers, such as construction workers and delivery riders. It turns weather forecasts into a plain-language heat plan and warns about waterlogged roads and underpasses.
about.stat1: Several parts of Delhi crossed 46 °C on 22 May 2026.
about.stat2: Traffic Police flagged 169 waterlogging-prone hotspots in 2026.
about.stat3: The ILO projects India loses 5.8% of working hours to heat by 2030.
about.heatIntro: Each hour of the forecast gets one band, using wet-bulb temperature (heat plus humidity) and air temperature. The first rule that matches wins:
about.heatRed: wet-bulb at least 30 °C or temperature at least 44 °C
about.heatOrange: wet-bulb at least 28 °C or temperature at least 40 °C
about.heatYellow: wet-bulb at least 25 °C or temperature at least 37 °C
about.escalation1: Hot nights: when the night stays at or above 30 °C, the body cannot recover, so the band rises.
about.escalation2: Heat streaks: the third ORANGE day in a row raises the band.
about.escalation3: Personal profile: heavy work or health conditions shared in the chat can raise the band for that person.
about.floodFormula: risk = min(1, susceptibility × rain factor + antecedent bonus)
about.floodExplain: Susceptibility comes from how often a spot appears on official hotspot lists (underpasses score higher). The rain factor comes from forecast rain in the next 1 and 3 hours. The antecedent bonus is added after heavy rain in the last 24 hours.
about.floodLevels: The risk score maps to LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH or SEVERE. A spot becomes CONFIRMED when a verified photo report is within 300 m in the last 2 hours.
about.srcOpenMeteo: Weather forecasts and historical reanalysis: Open-Meteo.com, licensed CC BY 4.0.
about.srcOsm: Map data: © OpenStreetMap contributors, licensed ODbL.
about.srcMapAmazon: Map tiles and style: Amazon Location Service.
about.srcMapOfm: Map tiles and style: OpenFreeMap (OpenMapTiles schema).
about.srcHotspots: Waterlogging hotspots: public lists from Delhi Traffic Police and civic agencies, as reported in the news.
about.limit1: All weather values are modelled data, not readings from weather stations.
about.limit2: Hotspot lists change every year, so some waterlogging spots may be missing.
about.limit3: JalTaap is not an official warning service. Follow IMD and Delhi government advisories.
about.team: Built by Team DevCore for Environmental Hacks (Heat & Water track).
